neighbours.label: the decimal point inside a 95% confidence interval or ratio statistic in medical results
fire: Smokers had a higher risk of relapse (hazard ratio 1.62, 95% CI 1.21 to 2.17; P = .002).
The odds of infection were lower in the vaccinated group (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.29-0.67).
Remission was more frequent with the new drug (RR 1.85, 95% CI 1.12 to 3.06).
Mortality was reduced in treated patients (HR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.58-0.87; p<0.001).
Children with asthma were more likely to be admitted (odds ratio 2.31, 95% confidence interval 1.40 to 3.81).
The incidence rate was 4.27 per 1000 person-years (95% CI 3.65-4.98) in the cohort.
Obesity was associated with recurrence (adjusted HR 1.39 [95% CI, 1.08-1.79], P = .01).
Overall survival improved with surgery (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.84; I2 = 12%).
quiet: Smokers had a higher risk of relapse, according to the doctors who ran the study.
The vaccinated group had fewer infections, and the nurses reported fewer side effects.
Remission was more frequent with the new drug, which pleased the patients' families.
Mortality was reduced in treated patients, although many still needed long hospital stays.
Children with asthma were more likely to be admitted during the cold winter months.
The clinic recorded about four new cases each year among the people in the cohort.
Obesity was associated with recurrence, so the team advised regular exercise and diet.
Overall survival improved with surgery, and most patients went home within a week.
